notes:
I don't have any notes for you yet. I tried to load six commentary pages (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, the Ellicott, Pulpit and Gill commentaries on Bible Hub, and Matthew Henry on StudyLight), but my script crashed while reading what came back. The tool then refused to let me run anything else, so I couldn't read any of those pages.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything, rather than give you points I can't source.

If you ask again, I'll start over:
1. **Main reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit commentaries on Bible Hub and StudyLight.
2. **Where traditions differ:** pages from the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites. Likely topics are the worldwide judgment in vv. 2–3 and 18, what "the Day of the LORD" means (vv. 7, 14–16), the "sacrifice" and "guests" in v. 7, and Milcom in v. 5.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (for example, the "foreign apparel" in v. 8 and "leaping over the threshold" in v. 9), and New Advent for Catholic readings. Zephaniah 1:14–16 is the source of the *Dies Irae*, so Catholic pages may well cover it.

The notes will be verse by verse ("v. 4: …") with a URL after every point, and I'll leave out any verse I can't find material on.
